scope: Business, scientific and project workbooks in the xlsx domain where the chart is the deliverable. The audit measures OOXML; a render or Excel export is still required before claiming visual quality.

notes.pie: Use only for 2–5 parts of a whole, never for ranking or more than 7 slices.
notes.bar: Sort categories by value unless the category order is meaningful.
notes.line: Use a date/numeric axis for time; do not connect categorical points that are not ordered.
notes.scatter: Use numeric X and Y columns; add a trendline only when the relationship is the message.
notes.combo: Use a secondary axis only when the units differ, and title both axes.
notes.waterfall: Start from a real total, keep one colour for increases and one for decreases, and label the bridge.
notes.histogram: State the bin width/count; do not use it for categories.
notes.box_whisker: State the quartile method and whether outliers/mean are shown.

rules.statement: Charts are at least 10×6 cm, fit the printable area, and use a stable aspect ratio.
rules.fix: Resize the chart frame; use a one-cell anchor.

rules.statement: Charts use a one-cell anchor with a fixed extent so row/column changes do not stretch them.
rules.fix: patch the drawing anchor; see chart_patch.py

rules.statement: Bar and column charts start at zero; a truncated axis exaggerates differences.
rules.fix: set the value axis minimum to 0 or use a dot plot

rules.statement: Log axes have base > 1 and a positive minimum; label the scale.
rules.fix: fix the scaling or use a linear axis

rules.statement: Each category has at least 0.55 cm of plot width; rotate or reduce labels when denser.
rules.fix: rotate labels, shorten names, or split the chart

rules.statement: Data labels use a readable size and do not collide with the line or axis title.
rules.fix: reduce labels, move the legend outside, or annotate only the key point

rules.statement: A legend is present for multiple series and does not cover the plot when there are many series.
rules.fix: move the legend below/right or direct-label series

rules.statement: Series colours have at least 3:1 contrast against the chart background.
rules.fix: darken the colour or add a border/marker

rules.statement: Adjacent series are distinguishable in normal vision and deuteranopia.
rules.fix: change the palette or add markers/patterns

rules.statement: The chart cache matches the worksheet values; stale caches are a common 'wrong chart' bug.
rules.fix: refresh/rebuild the chart or recalculate the workbook

rules.statement: Pie/doughnut charts have positive values, at most 7 slices, and a categorical palette.
No 3-D charts for quantitative comparison; they distort area and hide values.
The title states the insight and stays under 90 characters; the axis title carries the unit.
rules.fix: rewrite the title, move detail to a subtitle/source note

rules.statement: Every axis has a title with units; a secondary axis always has its own title.
rules.fix: add axis titles, including the secondary axis

rules.statement: The chart is inside the print area; the sheet is set to landscape/fit when needed.
rules.fix: set print area and orientation; do not clip the chart

rules.statement: The chart frame has alt text; a data table or direct labels provide a non-visual alternative.
rules.fix: set cNvPr descr/title; add direct labels

rules.statement: Chart text is at least 8 pt (10 pt title); use one family per workbook.
rules.fix: increase font sizes or reduce content

rules.statement: No more than 8 series in one chart; highlight one or use small multiples beyond that.
rules.fix: combine low-volume series, facet the chart, or highlight one line

standards.role: SpreadsheetML and DrawingML chart XML; anchors, chart caches and number formats.
Units, quantity symbols and decimal conventions in axis titles and labels.
Non-text contrast (1.4.11), use of colour (1.4.1), alt text (1.1.1), readable text.
Accessible chart alternatives in PDF/UA exports.
Visual display ergonomics for on-screen reading.
Colour-managed print and PDF/X export when the workbook is printed commercially.
